title: You didn’t wake up one day and decide to rebel.
paragraphs: You didn’t wake up one day and decide to rebel.
It was quieter than that.
It looked like prayer.
You had the plan mapped out—timelines, goals, outcomes. You even invited God into it. You said the right words. “Lord, bless this.” “God, make a way.” “Father, be with me.”
But deep down, you weren’t asking for His will.
You were asking for His approval.
And you knew it.
God saw it.
You kept moving forward, even when conviction whispered. Even when something in your spirit hesitated for a second… you pushed past it. Because the plan made sense. It was efficient. It was logical.
And it was yours.
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.” — Proverbs 3:5
Read that again.
Not some of your understanding.
Not most of it.
All your heart means surrender. Total dependence. The kind that feels like losing control.
But you didn’t want to lose control—you just wanted God to make your control work.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
So you kept going.
Doors opened, and you called it confirmation.
Opportunities came, and you called it favor.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Open doors are not always God’s doors.
“And a great door for effective work has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.” — 1 Corinthians 16:9
Not every “yes” is from heaven.
Sometimes God will let you walk through a door just to show you what life looks like without His covering.
And that’s where it starts to unravel.

Because the deeper you go into a God-less version of your God-invited plan, the heavier it feels. The pressure builds. The peace fades. You start striving for something that was never meant to be sustained by your strength.
You pray harder—but not differently.
Still asking Him to fix what He never initiated.
“Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I tell you?” — Luke 6:46
That question cuts deeper than most are willing to admit.
Because calling Him Lord means He leads.
Not advises.
Not assists.
Leads.
And if He’s not leading, then what you’re following isn’t Him.
It’s you.
God saw the moment you adjusted His instructions to fit your comfort.
You knew.
That relationship He told you to walk away from—you stayed.
That calling He placed in your heart—you delayed.
That sin you kept justifying—you renamed it.
And then you asked Him to bless it.
There’s a breaking point where the illusion shatters.
Where you realize you’ve been building something impressive… without God actually being at the center.
“For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul?” — Mark 8:36
Success without obedience is still loss.
Let that sit.
Because the scariest place to be isn’t failure.
It’s being successful outside of God’s will.
You look around, and everything seems intact—but something inside you knows…
This isn’t it.
That tension you feel? That restlessness you can’t explain?
That’s not random.
That’s mercy.
Because God doesn’t just expose sin—He invites you out of it.
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.” — Luke 9:23
Follow.
Not lead.
Not negotiate.
Follow.
And that’s where everything changes.
Because the Gospel isn’t God stepping into your story to improve it.
It’s Jesus ending your story—and giving you His.
You don’t tweak your plans.
You surrender them.
Completely.
Jesus didn’t go to the cross so you could have better outcomes.
He went so you could die to yourself and be raised into a life led by Him.
“I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me.” — Galatians 2:20
Read that again.
Not improved.
Not assisted.
Replaced.
That’s the invitation.
And that’s the cost.
So now you’re standing at a decision point, whether you admit it or not.
Keep asking God to follow your plans…
Or finally follow Him.
One leads to exhaustion dressed up as purpose.
The other leads to a cross… and then life.
Real life.
Peace that doesn’t depend on outcomes.
Direction that doesn’t rely on your understanding.
A relationship with God that isn’t built on convenience, but surrender.
The kind of faith most people talk about…
But never actually live.
You felt that for a reason.
Say it plainly—no filters, no pretending.
“I’ve been leading. Not following.”
Let that confession come out.
And if you’re tired of shallow faith and want deeper, consistent spiritual sharpening, step into what’s waiting for you here:
There’s more—truth that will confront you, rebuild you, and anchor you in Christ, not in yourself.
You’re going to need to read it again when the temptation to take control comes back.
Because it will.
And next time…
You’ll recognize it.
